steps.text: Blend the crema, cream cheese, and chicken bouillon in a blender until smooth; set aside.

Place the peppers on a large griddle over medium-high heat. Roast until the skin blisters and turns black. Remove peppers from griddle and place in a plastic bag, allowing them to sweat for 5 minutes. Transfer to a plate to cool. Peel and discard the outer skin of the peppers; halve length-wise and remove the seeds and veins. Slice into thick strips. Set aside.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat; cook the onion in the hot oil until tender, about 5 minutes. Stir the corn into the onions, reduce the heat to medium, and cook another 5 minutes. Add the poblano strips to the saucepan. Pour the cream mixture over the vegetables and bring to a simmer; cook at a simmer until hot, about 5 minutes more.

review.reviewBody: This dish was great! I followed the recipe exactly the way it is and I was so happy with the results. The corn was great in there too. It was my first time making rajas and my husband said they were delish! I felt so proud of myself. Serve with a side of beans and warm torillas for a full dinner. Provecho!

I have an abundance of poblano peppers in my garden (a veggie we are pretty new to), so I was looking for some new ways to eat them when I came across this recipe. Our entire family LOVED it!!! We just finished eating, and I already have requests for it again. My husband raved about it, something he almost never does, even about his favorite dishes. This dish is not too hot, something I appreciated. The corn balances the flavor of the peppers very nicely, and the sauce really cools down the hotness of the peppers. I *almost* made this exact to the recipe...there were a couple slight changes. First, I couldn't find Mexican crema, so I made my own (1 part sour cream to 4 parts light cream). Also, I only used about half the called for amount of cream cheese. It was perfect. I think (for us) the full amount would have been too much. We served this as a topping over chicken breasts that were salted, peppered, and cooked in a skillet, in butter and garlic. Delicious!!!

I made this for dinner and it was delicious. However, I did tweak the recipe a little bit. Rather than chicken bouillon, I sliced three chicken breasts and added to the onion and peppers after they had cooked down a little. I also doubled the amount of Crema to ensure there was enough sauce. It will be added to my "favorites" cookbook.

This are good! But my poblanos were not spicy at all! :( If you want them spicy you might want to try adding a couple serranos when roasting the chile, didn't use the griddle just put them under the broiler for couple min. just turn them over half way, I only used 1/4 of a cup of cream cheese in my opinion I don't think it needs the whole package unless you want them really creamy.Thanks Gema!

I didn't have crema on hand so I used sour cream and lemon juice. I added a few sliced roasted red peppers (jarred) for color as well. My poblanos were spicy but no one seemed to mind because this was so delicious! Will definitely do again!

I had purchased some Poblanos b/c they were on sale and wanted to do something different with them. I was just thinking "dip" when I made it, but after I made it (it was thicker than I expected) it hit me to add some chicken and made some enchiladas! I also added some jalapenos for some heat (Poblanos don't have "heat") and some SW seasoning. I made a simple cream sauce (using the Poblanos, chopped) topped it with some cheese and it was FANTASTIC!! Great for something different! Thank you for the recipe!!

Boy, oh, boy - this was the perfect recipe. I am newly married to a Mexican and although I am of Mexican heritage, I don't know much about Latin cuisine. But to my advantage, I love to eat and explore. Last weekend, I ate tamales de rajas. I loved this and this made me think. Although, I didn't want to attempt tamales, I wanted to incorporate rajas into my cooking.

I found this recipe and to make empanadas. I used the same basic recipe without adding corn. 
I made the empandada dough added a chuck of Queso Fresco and the rajas to the center and processed with traditional emapanadas. My husband loved this. Thank you for sharing this recipe with us. Because of this recipe, my husband will be taking this to his co-workers tomorrow to "show off" my cooking skills. AR is my secret - you make me look good. Thanks

I have a co-worker who's wife has made this for me occasionally over over years and I was wanting to learn to make it. I found this recipe and the picture looked very similar so I gave it a shot. The recipe was easy to follow and the dish easy to make. The only modifications I made were adding a few garlic cloves to the onions and adding a little cumin and cayenne pepper. This was awesome. Definitely making again. Thank you for the recipe!

Absolutely delicious! I've made many recipes from this website, but this is my first comment/review. I've made this recipe so many times that I feel I owe a review. If you like poblano peppers and anything creamy, then chances are you will love this recipe. My husband, who is from Mexico City, was pretty impressed the first time I made it, and so was I! It has made its way into our meal rotation. Now when I make it, i use regular sour cream because that's what we have on hand and only use half a pack of cream cheese instead of a whole. Another thing I love about this recipe is this is a dish that you can make ahead and tastes great the next day!
When I went to make this I realized I had no cream cheese. So, I left it out and upped the Mexican cream to 3/4 of a cup. Came out DELICIOUS!! We will be having this again soon.
I love this recipe as a side dish i use butter instead of oil and cut the cream cheese to half. Sometimes i also use it as a bed for pork chops yummy
Great! flavor . I used it as a sauce over backed chicken and it was a complete meal.

I followed this recipe from the magazine and ended up wasting my homegrown poblano peppers. The recipe here on this website is not the same as in the magazine especially when it comes down to how to roast the peppers. If you want to try this recipe do not cut the peppers in half because it’s not the same as cooking them whole to steam, then remove the skin. I should have known better because I work with poblano peppers all the time and I’ve never cut them before skinning them. Didn’t work at all.
I've been making this for nearly 20 yrs. It's hard to stop eating this. (El Gordo) at supper.
This was very good!

My husband and I are huge fans of poblano peppers so I was looking up recipes and came across this one. Decided to give it a go. I made it exact to the recipe and let me tell you IT WAS DELICIOUS!!! The only problem I had was peeling the skin after roasting them. But it was well worth it! I fried some potatoes with it and we put it all in tortillas and it was a huge hit! And we have plenty left for tomorrow! Such a great recipe that will be going into my permanent rotation!
Very easy to prepare and the taste was great!

Delicious!!! These rajas are so authentic. I had not had these in years and I had them for the first time this year when I went on vacation to Guadalajara, Mexico. These taste just like those. Sooo good!! I look forward to making them and can hardly wait until I do.
This was delicious, not enough for the serving size listed so I used 3 extra chiles.

Very Good! My first time roasting peppers, and the skin was really hard to get off!!! The only changes I might make next time might be to add chicken to make it a more rounded out meal for tortillas. I also think this would be great as more of a dip if the peppers were cut into bite size pieces instead of strips. Idk what I did wrong with the roasting of the peppers, but I may just saute them next time!!!
